matt: Seeing a weird perf regression on AMD pools after last night's autotune rollout. 95th latency up ~30% for seqlen > 1024 and KV cache hit rate dropped. Looks like some kernels weren't registered so we soft-fallback to a slow generic path. Anyone seen this?

sara: Which model and autotune profile? logs?

matt: gpt-7b-medium, autotuner picked `tiling_v2_int8`. Kernel registry shows no entry for `tile_kernel_v2_amdfp16` on mi250, so route -> generic_matmul (much slower). Sample log: 

```
[autotune] selected: tiling_v2_int8
[kernel_lookup] model:gpt-7b tag:tiling_v2_int8 arch:mi250 -> NOT_FOUND
[route] fallback: generic_matmul fp16
```

carla: Hm, could be the registration race or a conditional compile flag. We saw something similar where driver ABI mismatches caused symbol renames.

jamie: I profiled a few traces; KV hits dropped ~18% since rollout. Looks like batching heuristics changed and we're flushing prefixes when a kernel is missing.

jamie: snippet: 

```
KVCache.get(prefix_hash=0xabc4) -> MISS (expected HIT)
Batcher.flush_on_missing_kernel: true
```

matt: We didn't intend to change flush policy. Autotuner might have toggled `safe_flush_on_soft_route`. @infra-bot can you fetch the rollout diff?

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T02:14:22: diff: https://git.internal/redwood/autotune/rollouts/pr-842

sara: Looking at the PR - there's a new fallback_policy `soft-reroute-clear-cache` added in the routing layer. That explains KV invalidations.

matt: We should either revert that policy or change it to `hold-kv-on-soft-route`. We can't afford KV thrash for long-tail seqlen requests.

carla: Two action items: (1) kernel registry fix for the missing `tile_kernel_v2_amdfp16` (looks like mi250 node labels changed during node maintenance and registration skipped), (2) rollback the clear-cache behavior immediately.

jamie: I repro locally by forcing kernel absent: `python -m runtime.test_kernel_presence --arch mi250 --model gpt7b`. `kern_registry.lookup` returns None and dispatch falls back to generic path.

matt: Proposed immediate plan: 1) patch autotune to not clear KV on soft-route, 2) add telemetry for `kernel_missing` events (model, arch, seqlen_bucket), 3) schedule a hotfix to re-register kernels on affected pools this weekend.

sara: Opening issue #1147 with those tasks. I'll coordinate rollback and hotfix.

jamie: Extra perf note: dispatch time doubled on affected traces and we see ~18% more memcpy overhead due to repeated KV population cycles - flame shows `dispatch->prepare_kv->copy_prefix` hot.

carla: Long-term: autotuner should gate profile suggestions by kernel availability across target fleets and seqlen distribution. If tails exceed 1k tokens regularly, prefer profiles with broader kernel support. Also add a pre-rollout compatibility check that runs `kernel_registry.verify(profile)` against a sample of pools.

matt: :thumbsup: I'll roll a quick patch to revert the clear-cache flag and add the telemetry counter. Anyone object to immediate revert? @sara @carla

sara: No objections. Rolling back now and will open the hotfix runbook. ETA rollback: ~2h, registry fix: ~1 day.

infra-bot: Rollback started: deploy 2026-03-15T04:20:00 by sara, status: in-progress

matt: Thanks. Please post updates here if rollback doesn't restore pre-rollout perf. We'll follow-up in incidents if it's not resolved. :eyes:
